name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,525

clue.text: Occupies the mind, muscles and eyeballs

blocks.note: abs is the everyday short name for the abdominal muscles
orbs is a poetic word for eyes

explanation.surface: A description of something so gripping it seizes the brain, the body and the eyes all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Muscles and eyeballs sound like more things being occupied, but they simply build the word in two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that grips your attention completely is said to engross or hold you, the sense of this verb.

clue.text: Stuck in present occupying address

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit inside, so the word for present goes within the other piece

blocks.note: add. is the standard abbreviation for address
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck in a gift being delivered to an address.
explanation.walkthrough: Present suggests a gift; it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: To have clung or been fastened firmly to something is to have stuck to it.

clue.text: Takes part in sports teams

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, backs one party in a dispute
second meaning: the opposing teams in a game

explanation.surface: Someone competes in team games.
explanation.walkthrough: Takes part in reads as one phrase meaning participates; split it, and takes part means supports a faction.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means backing one faction, and the noun names the opposing teams in a match.

clue.text: Loaf said to be dry and seeded

indicators.note: said tells us we hear these words spoken, so their sounds count, not their spellings

blocks.note: dry humour is wry; the grain sounds the same
seeded means sown, produced, bred; the staple food sounds the same

explanation.surface: A description of a dry loaf with seeds in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry and seeded read as describing the loaf; each is a sound-alike for one half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made with flour from this cereal grain is baked as a dense, dark loaf.

clue.text: Potboilers built up into epic tale

indicators.note: in a down clue, built up means the word rises from the bottom, so it is read upward

blocks.note: an Aga is a heavy British range cooker on which pots boil

explanation.surface: Cheap pulp novels are expanded into a grand story.
explanation.walkthrough: Potboilers are usually hack-written books; here they are literally things that boil pots.
explanation.definitionFit: The word first named Norse heroic narratives and now means any long, sprawling story.

clue.text: Nasty red-backed snake

indicators.note: something backed has gone into reverse, so the colour word is read from its end

blocks.note: mean means unkind or nasty
taken as written before it turns round

explanation.surface: A warning about a vicious snake with a red back.
explanation.walkthrough: Snake looks like a noun for a reptile, but it is the verb: to wind about.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to follow a winding, twisting course, just as a lazy river wanders across a plain.

clue.text: Mother elephant catching a whiff of human's incomprehensible speech

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the smell abbreviation goes between the two family words

blocks.note: mum is the British word for mother
BO, body odour, is the smell of an unwashed person
Jumbo was a famous Victorian circus elephant, and the name stands for any elephant

explanation.surface: A mother elephant smells a person and starts speaking gibberish.
explanation.definitionFit: This rhyming phrase means meaningless jargon or nonsense, especially pseudo-mystical talk designed to confuse.

clue.text: Beasts of burden at square price

blocks.note: asses, or donkeys, carry loads
S as a short form for square, as in street names abbreviated Sq

explanation.surface: Pack animals are sold for a fair price.
explanation.walkthrough: Price is the verb here, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To price something is to estimate or set its value, which is to evaluate it.

clue.text: Drier, meaning unusual conditions for accidents

indicators.note: unusual conditions mean an altered state, so the next word's letters are set out differently

blocks.note: the nine letters of this word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A road-safety note: drier weather means unusual conditions for crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: Drier looks like a comparative adjective; it is a noun, a drying agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance such as silica gel that absorbs moisture is a drying agent.

clue.text: Old record sure is broken with style, ultimately

indicators.note: broken things lie in pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a fresh order
ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the word before is kept

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, to be jumbled
the final letter of style

explanation.surface: A collector insists that an old vinyl record is cracked, though stylishly.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is an earlier album or single released again, so it is an old recording brought back.

clue.text: Husband dined out on lettuce, an unexpected treat

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of dined are put in another order

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
the letters of this word, to be rearranged
Little Gem is a small variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: A husband eats out on a salad, which turns out to be a pleasant surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Dined out reads as a restaurant visit; out is really the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A little-known place or thing that proves delightful once discovered is called by this idiom.

clue.text: Gives us hiccups to swallow Asian food

indicators.note: the phrase gulps the wanted word down inside itself, so it sits within the run of letters

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of us and the start of hiccups

explanation.surface: Someone complains that trying to swallow a certain dish brings on hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish is one of the best-known foods of Asia.

clue.text: A sorry ragged string of beads

indicators.note: ragged means torn and disordered, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the six letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shabby, tattered necklace is described with pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholics use a looped string of prayer beads to count their prayers, and that is what this word names.

clue.text: Bags of lettuce for Russian peasants?

blocks.note: cos is a long-leaved lettuce, also called romaine
sacks are large bags

explanation.surface: Sacks of salad greens are handed out to the peasantry of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads bags first, but the lettuce comes first in the answer; the question mark admits that these horsemen were not strictly peasants.
explanation.definitionFit: These were free peoples of the southern Russian steppe, often of humble farming stock and famed as cavalry.

clue.text: Given name Setter would change for definite

indicators.note: change asks for the following word's letters to be altered into a new order

blocks.note: the setter speaks of themselves as I, and I would contracts to I'd
the letters of this word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter muses about swapping a vague name for a definite one.
explanation.walkthrough: Given name suggests a forename; read it as having been given a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been named or recognised has been pinned down by their identity.

clue.text: On record and on sale in Paris and London, perhaps

definitions.note: not a synonym: it completes the title of George Orwell's memoir, so the answer is the missing start of that title

blocks.note: something put down is written into the record
taken as written
a book or record that is out has been released for sale

explanation.surface: A recording is said to be available in shops in two great capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Orwell wrote Down and Out in Paris and London about his years of poverty; the clue supplies the end of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means destitute and homeless, the condition Orwell lived and described in those two cities.

clue.text: Marsupials consisting of dam perhaps with uninitiated offspring

indicators.note: uninitiated suggests having no beginning, so the first letter of the young ones is lost

blocks.note: a dam is a kind of wall holding back water
babies are offspring

explanation.surface: Marsupials are described as a mother animal and her inexperienced young.
explanation.walkthrough: Dam suggests a mother animal next to offspring; it is a barrier holding back water.
explanation.definitionFit: These small Australian relatives of the kangaroo carry their young in a pouch, so they are marsupials.

clue.text: Cabbage as starter for knockwurst and beer

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter of the sausage word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of knockwurst
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A German meal: cabbage served first with sausage and beer.
explanation.definitionFit: This leafy green is a variety of the cabbage family, grown for its curly leaves.

clue.text: American police department deliberately lose location of worst offenders

blocks.note: the DEA is the US Drug Enforcement Administration
to throw a match is to lose it on purpose

explanation.surface: A US police department deliberately loses track of where its most dangerous criminals are held.
explanation.definitionFit: The cells holding prisoners awaiting execution house those convicted of the gravest crimes.

clue.text: Cabbage preferred by old king?

blocks.note: first meaning: an old word for cabbage, surviving in coleslaw
second meaning: the name that has Old King placed in front of it in the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A question about which vegetable an elderly monarch liked best.
explanation.walkthrough: Preferred looks like liking; read it as pre-ferred, placed before: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old name for brassicas such as cabbage, and also the surname of the rhyme's jolly monarch.

clue.text: Lucky me, tucking into edible leaf

indicators.note: tucking into puts the first word snugly inside the leaf vegetable

blocks.note: chard is a leafy vegetable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks themselves fortunate to be eating leafy greens.
explanation.walkthrough: Tucking into suggests eating, but it means placing inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A life that seems protected by magic or good fortune is said to be blessed in this way.

clue.text: Wanting an appearance that confounds innate bias

indicators.note: to confound is to throw into confusion, so the letters that follow are mixed up

blocks.note: the ten letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A psychologist notes that inborn prejudice can undermine a hoped-for impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Wanting an appearance reads as desiring one; it means lacking one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase describes something done while the person concerned is not present, lacking their attendance.

clue.text: Preacher perhaps bitter when entertaining afterwards

indicators.note: to entertain is to host someone inside, so the beer word holds the time word

blocks.note: bitter is a British style of ale
post is Latin for after, as in post-war

explanation.surface: A preacher becomes bitter when he has to entertain guests later on.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter reads as resentful; in Britain it is a type of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ's twelve followers went out preaching, and the word extends to any ardent advocate of a cause.

clue.text: River mammals in rocks, hiding head

indicators.note: hiding its head means the first letter of the verb is concealed and dropped

blocks.note: rocks as a verb means sways unsteadily, totters

explanation.surface: Animals of the riverbank lurk among the stones with their heads hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocks looks like stones by a river; it is the verb, to sway.
explanation.definitionFit: These sleek aquatic members of the weasel family live along rivers and catch fish.

clue.text: An animal uprising, overturning slaughterhouse

indicators.note: overturning turns the uprising word upside down, which in an across clue means reading it backwards

blocks.note: the indefinite article as a single letter
a bat is an animal
a riot is a violent uprising

explanation.surface: An Animal Farm scene: the beasts rise up and overthrow the slaughterhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word names the building where animals are killed for meat.

clue.text: Wounds receding care of plaster

indicators.note: something receding moves back, so the word for wounds runs backwards

blocks.note: cuts are wounds
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: Healing injuries are tended with a plaster dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaster suggests a sticking plaster on a wound, but it is the building material.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine render or plaster is applied to walls and ceilings, often moulded decoratively.

clue.text: Popstar touring England to sound of appreciative audience

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the singer wraps around the country abbreviation

blocks.note: Cher is the American pop singer
E is the abbreviation for England

explanation.surface: A pop star tours England and the crowds roar their approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy crowd's shout of approval or encouragement is a hurrah or roar of applause.

clue.text: Special prize for showing agility

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for special
to prize, or prise, open is to lever, which Americans call pry

explanation.surface: An award is given for nimble performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Prize looks like an award; it is the verb meaning to lever open.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person who is active and nimble on their feet is described as lively in this way.

clue.text: Part of America where lettuce hasn't run out

indicators.note: hasn't says the salad word is missing something, namely the cricket abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: romaine is the American name for cos lettuce
RO is the scorecard abbreviation for run out in cricket

explanation.surface: A US state where the salad supply has never dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: Run out sounds like supplies being exhausted; it is a cricket dismissal, abbreviated RO on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-eastern state of the USA is one of the fifty that make up the country.

clue.text: Deficient naughty child fine with standing around

indicators.note: around says the upright word surrounds the abbreviation for fine

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
erect means standing upright
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A teacher's report on a badly behaved child who is fine standing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawed or lacking in some respect falls short of being whole or faultless.

clue.text: Put down round tube that's empty

indicators.note: round says the put-down word is wrapped about the letter for the tube

blocks.note: to diss is slang for to insult or put down
a U-tube is bent into the shape of the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone talks down about an empty London Underground train.
explanation.walkthrough: Tube suggests the Underground, but here it is the bent U-tube of the laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A building no longer used stands empty, abandoned and out of service.

clue.text: Plant by seawater never appearing evenly

indicators.note: evenly picks only the letters in even positions, the second, fourth and so on

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and later even-numbered letters of these words

explanation.surface: A plant that grows beside salt water but never shows itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen conifer, common in churchyards, is a plant in the broad botanical sense.
